what: an R1 round on the edge where a 1 mm chamfer round the bottom of a 45 mm extrusion meets its side walls; the outline (three circles joined by a polyline, its one sharp corner rounded R2) is tangent-continuous, so the chamfer and the round each run round it as one chain (the reporter's script, unchanged)
method: Outline: the boundary of the union of circles R30.475 at (-8,0), R15.5 at (-22.975,-51.975) and (7,-51.975) and the hexagon of the script's polyline; the last polyline side is tangent to the right-hand R15.5 and enters the R30.475 at (6.9735,-26.5428), a concave corner the R2 fillet rounds (centre (9.9163,-27.0856), tangent points (8.3320,-28.3062) on the line and (8.8129,-25.4175) on the arc, 94.127 deg). Its area by Green's theorem over its lines and arcs A0 = 5191.734097 mm2, its length L0 = 287.842541 mm, total turning 2 pi. Every radius of curvature of the outline (15.5, 30.475 convex; 2 concave) is larger than the 1 mm the blends reach in, so a section s swept along the outline at inset centroid distance d removes area(s) (L0 - 2 pi d) (the inset curve at d has length L0 - 2 pi d). Extrusion V0 = 45 A0 = 233628.0344. The 1 mm chamfer: the triangle of legs 1, area 1/2, centroid 1/3 in: 0.5 (L0 - 2 pi/3) = 142.8741; V1 = 233485.1603. The R1 round between the wall and the 45 deg chamfer face (135 deg between them): section area r2 (tan(pi/8) - pi/8) = 0.02151448, its centroid 0.060165 mm in from the wall (first moment of the region between the wall, the chamfer line and the ball of centre (1, sqrt 2)); removed 0.02151448 (L0 - 2 pi 0.060165) = 6.1846; V = 233478.9756 mm3.
